items.title: ssh/tailssh, tstest/natlab/vmtest: expand Tailscale SSH test coverage
items.body:
Add Docker integration tests for TCP and Unix forwarding, pty size,
resize and modes, session env, envknobs, x11 rejection, session
teardown, SessionDuration, policy changes and RuleExpires on active
sessions, Shutdown, host keys and utmp, and run every integrationtest
test in the Dockerfile. Extend the vmtest SSH tests to use real
OpenSSH clients across the tailnet for pty, sftp/scp, agent and port
forwarding, AcceptEnv, ControlMaster, large transfers, banners, user
mapping, revocation, check mode (via a new testcontrol handler),
recording, and the tailscale ssh CLI. Fix make sshintegrationtest,
which only ever tested one image and always exited 0, and trigger the
workflow on go.mod changes and a schedule.

items.title: ipn/ipnlocal: avoid authoritative ExtraRecord routes with default DNS
items.body:
Fixes #21787

## Change
- Skip synthesized authoritative ExtraRecord routes when quad-100 already uses default resolvers so unknown descendants remain eligible for upstream forwarding
- Apply the same rule after exit-node fallback selection while preserving explicit control routes and existing no-default scoping
- Add one end-to-end DNS regression and extend existing exit-node tests

## Local Validation
- Original issue regression fails before the fix and passes afterward for Linux, Windows and Darwin configuration variants
- Related package tests pass on macOS and Linux, including `./tool/go test ./ipn/ipnlocal ./net/dns/... -count=1` on macOS
- `./tool/go test -race ./ipn/ipnlocal ./net/dns/... -count=1` passes on macOS and Windows compile-only checks pass
- Standard vet, staticcheck, gofmt, goimports and PR-style golangci-lint pass with zero new issues

Full unfiltered golangci-lint retains two existing inline diagnostics and Darwin custom vet retains five existing subtest-name diagnostics, both reproduced unchanged on clean baseline `afe142bc876952fd3e7f14b6284036228ca3af20`

items.title: ssh/tailssh: route SSH forwarding through the privileged monitor
items.body:
Route tailssh's forwarding through the per-connection ssh-monitor, so on unix forwarded sockets are dialed and bound by children with the authenticated local user's credentials, never by root tailscaled.

- unix -L, direct-streamlocal: the lexical allowlist check stays in tailscaled as coarse policy. The allowlist is home, /tmp, and /run/user/<uid>. Relative and abstract paths are rejected. The dial then runs as the user through the monitor. The EvalSymlinks re-validation is dropped, and the kernel's DAC is the boundary. The allowlist is capped. A home directory that cleans to "/" or is empty would prefix-match every absolute path, and such an entry is dropped instead. Paths at or beyond the sun_path capacity reject lexically rather than dying at bind or dial with a generic EINVAL.
- unix -R, streamlocal-forward: the listener is created by a user-cred child with umask-at-bind 0600 and unlink-if-owned. Closing it does not unlink the socket, and the stale file on cancel is accepted.
- TCP -R, tcpip-forward: a tailssh-owned handler replaces gliderssh's ForwardedTCPHandler. The bind goes through the monitor's listen op with the local user's credentials, so privileged ports fail by kernel construction for non-root-mapped users. Root-mapped users are allowed, as in OpenSSH. Bind addresses are loopback-only unless TS_SSH_FORWARD_GATEWAY_PORTS is set, the equivalent of sshd's GatewayPorts.
- agent forwarding: the socket and its containing directory are created by a user-cred child, a 0600 socket in a 0700 user-owned directory, instead of a root-run MkdirTemp, Chmod, and Chown sequence. Session-end cleanup is unchanged.

The monitor is spawned lazily on the first forwarding or agent need, from the tailscaled binary, and closed when the SSH connection ends. closeFwdMonitor latches a closed flag under the fwd lock, so a caller racing the teardown is refused by fwdMonitor, or reads the current state without spawning through fwdMonitorIfAny, instead of respawning a monitor nobody ever closes.

plan9 keeps today's behavior through a build-tagged seam, fwdmonitor.go and fwdplan9.go. There is no monitor on plan9. Unix forwarding is rejected there, and reverse TCP forwarding keeps the gliderssh handler with the mayReversePortForwardTo gate.

Tests cover conn-level callbacks against a real monitor and real one-shot fwd children: allowlist rejections, user-owned 0600 sockets, a foreign sticky-dir socket not unlinked, loopback, gateway-ports, and privileged-port TCP binds, agent directory hygiene and cleanup, and TS_SSH_DISABLE_FORWARDING coverage, plus refused respawn after teardown. The unix-fwd root-dial regressions cover a static in-allowlist symlink to a root-owned 0600 canary, which must fail permission denied as the bound user, and a dir-swap race, which must never serve the protected canary.

Updates tailscale/corp#50380

items.title: ssh/tailssh: add user-credential forwarding children and monitor dial/listen ops
items.body:
Add the one-shot "be-child ssh-fwd" children that perform forwarded socket work, and the monitor and client plumbing for the socket ops. The conn and session flows do not use the ops yet. The next commit routes them.

- fwdchild.go: a child re-execed by the monitor, born unprivileged at clone. The monitor applies the connection's bound identity as SysProcAttr.Credential, so the kernel's DAC sees the connection user's permissions. It dials a unix socket, or creates one with umask-at-bind mode and optional unlink-if-owned, or binds a TCP listener, or creates the agent-forwarding socket in a user-owned directory. The result returns to the monitor over an inherited socketpair as one status line with at most one descriptor attached.
- monitor.go: handleDial and handleListen run the ops on one-shot children with a spawn-to-result deadline, monFwdOpDeadline. On expiry the child's group is SIGKILLed. killChild reaps such a child with a bounded non-blocking wait. A child left in uninterruptible sleep is abandoned in its own group rather than blocking the loop goroutine. The dial and listen placeholder replies are gone, and their not-implemented test with them.
- monitor_client.go: Dial, Listen, and ListenAgent over the existing request-ID plumbing.
- incubator.go, monitor_linux.go, monitor_other.go: registration and per-platform spawn attributes for the fwd children.

Tests drive real children across uid boundaries. They cover dial and bind round trips, unix and TCP listens, agent-listen directory hygiene, unlink-if-owned, peer-credential assertions, and the no-identity-keys-on-the-wire shape of every request.

Updates tailscale/corp#50380

items.title: ssh/tailssh: relay Unix forward payloads as the bound user
items.body:
Keep the dialed service socket in the credentialed forwarding child and return a private socketpair endpoint instead. Passing the service socket to tailscaled preserves connect-time peer credentials but causes payload SCM_CREDENTIALS to identify the root daemon.

Keep dial children alive for bidirectional forwarding. Return a lifetime
pipe alongside the data socket so full closure or a discarded dial reply
ends the relay independently of data EOF. Preserve half-closes and the
monitor's descriptor acknowledgment/teardown ownership for both fds.
Listener children retain their existing descriptor handoff behavior.

Handle local Unix forwarding channel closure independently of the SSH
connection: the channel request stream closes on CHANNEL_CLOSE, not
CHANNEL_EOF. Stop waiting for service output while giving queued client
payload a bounded drain in each forwarding stage, so a silent or
non-reading service cannot retain the relay indefinitely.

Test relay exit/reaping with silent services, discarded replies, queued
payload and backpressure, including end-to-end SSH channel closure while
the transport stays connected. Fix a canary test's unsynchronized marker
assertion to wait for the reporting goroutine.

Add a root-run cross-UID SO_PASSCRED regression test and lifecycle coverage for both half-close directions and monitor shutdown with an idle relay.

Updates tailscale/corp#50380

Signed-off-by: James Tucker <james@tailscale.com>

items.title: ssh/tailssh: dial TCP forwards as the bound user
items.body:
Route direct-tcpip channels, used by TCP -L and SOCKS -D forwards, through the per-connection monitor after the existing policy checks. Resolve names and create/connect TCP sockets in a child running with the authenticated local user credentials instead of the root daemon.

Hand the connected TCP descriptor back through the existing acknowledged fd protocol. TCP socket ownership survives the handoff, so UID-based firewall policy sees the mapped user. TCP has no per-message SCM_CREDENTIALS and needs no persistent relay: the child exits after handing off the socket. Bound resolution/dialing by the monitor forwarding deadline.

Share the channel-close-aware forwarding copy loop with Unix forwards, retaining bidirectional half-closes and bounded draining on full close. Plan 9 retains its existing in-process forwarding path.

Add root-run IPv4/IPv6 socket-owner regression tests, hostname and half-close coverage, policy/disable gates, invalid/refused dial handling, and a pin that the child is reaped while its socket remains usable. Update the TCP policy revocation fixture for child spawning and synchronize its assertion on transport shutdown.

Updates tailscale/corp#50380

Signed-off-by: James Tucker <james@tailscale.com>

items.title: ssh/tailssh: enforce SSH policy at the connection level
items.body:
Re-evaluate authenticated connections on policy updates and at session
and forwarding gates. Close connections whose grants are revoked or
narrowed, including forwarding permissions, user identity, duration,
AcceptEnv, and effective recording requirements. Recheck rule-derived
AcceptEnv and recording configuration for delegated connections too.

Treat recording-failure changes in either direction as material,
including fail-open to fail-closed transitions. An inconclusive user
lookup retains the previous identity but does not skip other policy
checks. An absent account revokes the connection.

Re-arm rule-expiry timers under the policy recheck lock and prevent
re-arming after teardown. Add connection-level login grace, extending
it during delegation and stopping it only on SSH authentication
success, not on unsigned key queries or partial authentication.
Close the raw transport and cancel delegated authentication on teardown.

Add regression tests for these transitions and remove scheduling
assumptions from delegation tests.

items.title: ssh/tailssh: name the monitor for its connection-wide role
items.body:
Move lazy monitor startup, credentials, and cleanup into connmonitor.go and rename the connection state and accessors. The monitor owns session processes as well as forwarding children. Move the session exit registry alongside session monitor handling and keep the Plan 9 stub in a matching file.

Update callers, tests, and diagnostic prefixes without changing monitor lifecycle behavior.

items.title: ssh/tailssh: add ssh-monitor process and client
items.body:
Add the monitor core. It is the per-connection privileged "tailscaled be-child ssh-monitor" process, plus tailscaled's client for it. New code plus childproc registration only. No existing conn, session, or forwarding flow calls the monitor yet. Later commits wire those.

- monitor.go: identity is bound at spawn in argv. The event loop waits on inbound RPC frames from a dedicated reader goroutine, on external SIGHUP, and on SIGCHLD. Child exits wake the loop as SIGCHLD, and the sweep reaps what is ready with wait4(WNOHANG) and emits unsolicited exit notifications, so an idle monitor sleeps in its read with no polling. On EOF, error, or external SIGHUP it SIGHUPs every child group, reaps briefly, then SIGKILLs every remembered group and reaps again. The inherited RPC fd is close-on-exec at entry. Per-op spawn-and-reply deadlines have bounded reaping, so an uninterruptible child can never wedge the loop. ping, exec, and signal are implemented. dial and listen parse and reply a descriptive not-implemented error until the forwarding wiring lands. Signal pids are validated against the monitor's own children. exec requires an absolute argv[0] and maps SCM_RIGHTS stdio to 0..2. monStdio owns every descriptor it is given. On error it closes them all, and the caller must not touch them again.
- monitor_linux.go and monitor_other.go: per-platform child SysProcAttr. Own process group, or Setsid+Setctty with the pty slave as fd 0 for ctty children. Linux-only Pdeathsig, documented as advisory.
- monitor_client.go: spawnMonitor re-execs the current binary, sets up the socketpair via ExtraFiles, and runs the monitor in its own session with close-on-exec hygiene at both ends. monitorClient serializes writes, keeps a request-ID table with per-call context deadlines, delivers unsolicited exit notifications to a registered callback, and closes via the monitor's own EOF teardown.
- monitor_rpc.go: add the exec reply constructor.
- incubator.go: register the ssh-monitor be-child handler.

Tests drive a real monitor child. The client re-execs the test binary through a spawn-prefix seam, and the helper test dispatches to beMonitor. They cover ping and exec round-trip, fd leak and CLOEXEC, group signal with pid validation, error propagation, not-implemented replies, EOF and SIGHUP teardown with the spawned child's death asserted directly, and identity binding.

Updates tailscale/corp#50380

items.title: tsnet: authorize ListenSSH peers, fix PTY emulation and session queue bound
items.body:
ListenSSH's trust model is now documented prominently: sessions are
gated only on the peer's Tailscale identity (a successful WhoIs); there
is no SSH-level client authentication, no SSHPolicy evaluation, no
local user mapping, and no session recording. Embedders that need more
than trusted-tailnet-peer semantics must gate sessions themselves, and
the new opt-in Server.SSHAuthCallback is the recommended way: sessions
from peers it denies are refused at session open (exit 1) instead of
being yielded to Accept. It is plumbed through LocalBackend.ListenSSH
and the HookListenSSH hook; with no callback, behavior is unchanged.

Also for the ListenSSH SSH server (session channels only, no
forwarding):

- PTY sessions are delivered raw: DisablePTYEmulation is now called on
  every session, so a net.Conn consumer never gets \n -> \r\n
  translation (binary passthrough was being corrupted). Session.Pty()
  also forwards window changes best-effort (drop when undrained) so a
  non-draining consumer can't wedge gliderssh's per-session request
  loop through the window-change handler.

- A handshake that never completes is bounded (HandshakeTimeout, via
  the TS_SSH_LOGIN_GRACE_TIME knob, default 120s). TS_SSH_IDLE_TIMEOUT
  (a Go duration or bare seconds; "0" disables) bounds protocol-idle
  connections (no SSH traffic at all; any traffic resets it) for both
  SSH servers. It is off by default: gliderssh resets it solely on
  transport reads/writes, so it would otherwise close legitimately
  idle sessions and established port-forwards that carry no traffic.

- At most 16 accepted-but-unconsumed sessions park in the listener's
  queue; if the application stops calling Accept, further sessions are
  refused instead of parking an unbounded number of goroutines.

Updates tailscale/corp#50380

items.title: ssh/tailssh: add monitor RPC codec and SCM_RIGHTS fd passing
items.body:
New self-contained code for the per-connection privileged ssh-monitor. No existing behavior or wiring changes. Later commits wire the forwarding and session paths onto it.

rpcFrame is the newline-delimited JSON wire struct with request IDs. It covers dial, listen, exec, signal, and ping requests, ok and err replies, and unsolicited exit notifications. rpcConn is the framing codec over one socketpair end. Reads go only through ReadMsgUnix with a CmsgSpace(3*sizeof(int)) OOB buffer. A plain Read or an undersized buffer silently drops ancillary data, and the kernel closes the dropped descriptors. A stream read never returns data beyond an SCM_RIGHTS-carrying message, so a descriptor arrives with the first chunk of a split line and survives reassembly. Writes attach descriptors to the first byte of a line and never to an empty payload. A short write resends the remainder as plain data, because resending the ancillary data would duplicate the descriptors. Received descriptors are marked close-on-exec at parse time, by the codec rather than by the stdlib's platform-dependent handling. Lines are capped at 256 KiB, and NUL bytes and frames carrying more descriptors than their op declares are rejected on receive. A read timeout returns os.ErrDeadlineExceeded and preserves any partially received line, so the monitor's poll loop can sweep between reads without losing the frame. A read timeout is the only error that preserves state. Every other error closes all held descriptors and clears the buffer.

sendFds, recvFds, and wrapUnixConn are shared by the monitor and client sides. wrapUnixConn consumes its fd, because os.NewFile's finalizer cannot be neutralized from outside.

Tests exercise ping and fd round-trips with liveness and FD_CLOEXEC checks, multi-fd frames, kernel framing pins for first-chunk ancillary delivery and undersized-OOB MSG_CTRUNC rejection, 64 KiB-plus split-line reassembly under a shrunken SO_SNDBUF, oversized and NUL rejection, the short-write resend path, the read-timeout state-preservation contract, and 50-way multiplexed request/reply traffic.
